children: The UK Nationwide House Price Index rose 1.6% year-on-year in August 2026, following a revised 1.4% increase in July and coming in below the expected 2.1% gain.

Nationwide Chief Economist Robert Gardner said market activity and house prices have remained subdued in recent months amid an uncertain economic backdrop, with Middle East tensions pushing up energy prices and contributing to volatility in market interest rate expectations.
However, moderating private-sector wage growth and signs that higher energy costs have not yet fed into underlying price pressures could give the Bank of England more room to assess policy.
Gardner noted that affordability is improving as house price growth remains well below earnings growth, although higher mortgage rates have offset some of the gains.
He added that activity could regain momentum if the energy shock fades and market interest rates decline.
On a monthly basis, house prices grew 0.2%, following a 0.1% fall in July.

title: UK House Price Growth Falls Short of Forecast
